t: A mountain kingdom centred on Lake Van, called Biainili by its own kings, that rivalled Assyria in the 9th–7th centuries BCE.
Its kings built rock fortresses, storehouses and canals; Menua’s canal still carries water to the city of Van.
Weakened by Assyria and Cimmerians, Urartu vanished around 590 BCE, and its lands became the Armenian heartland.
dyk: Yerevan, capital of modern Armenia, traces its origin to the Urartian fortress of Erebuni, founded by Argishti I in 782 BCE, and celebrated its 2,750th anniversary in 1968.
ev: Shalmaneser III of Assyria sacks Arzashkun, royal city of King Arame
Sarduri I builds the citadel of Tushpa on the rock of Van
Argishti I founds the fortress of Erebuni, origin of Yerevan
Tiglath-pileser III defeats Sarduri II and his Syrian allies
Sargon II defeats Rusa I and sacks the temple of Haldi at Musasir
Rusa II founds Teishebaini, Bastam, Ayanis and Rusahinili
Urartu disappears, probably conquered by the Medes

f.capital: Arzashkun (under Arame); from c. 840 BCE Tushpa (Van)
